films.title: Paranormal Activity
films.yearNote: Festival premiere at Screamfest Oct 14, 2007; limited US release Sept 25, 2009; nationwide Oct 16, 2009
films.villain: Unseen demonic presence that has haunted Katie since childhood and feeds on negative energy
notes: Produced, written, directed, photographed and edited by Oren Peli
Shot for $15,000 on a home video camera, mostly on a tripod
Acquired by DreamWorks (then a Paramount subsidiary); new ending cost an additional $200,000
Original ending shown only at 2007 Screamfest; two new endings developed after the acquisition
~$108M US and ~$85M international
Often cited as most profitable film by return on investment, though hard to verify; first of the series

films.title: Hellboy
films.writers: del Toro (story: del Toro, Peter Briggs)
films.basedOn: Hellboy comic by Mike Mignola (Dark Horse Comics)
films.villain: Grigori Rasputin, resurrected by Ilsa von Haupstein and Kroenen to trigger the apocalypse via Hellboy
notes: Premiered March 30, 2004 at Mann Village Theater; US release April 2, 2004
Draws on the comic Hellboy: Seed of Destruction
Karel Roden plays Rasputin; Doug Jones plays Abe Sapien (voiced uncredited by David Hyde Pierce)
Hellboy works for the Bureau of Paranormal Research and Defense
Followed by Hellboy II: The Golden Army (2008)

films.title: Red Eye
films.villain: Jackson Rippner, operative of a domestic terrorist group plotting to assassinate a Homeland Security official
notes: Described by trades as Phone Booth on a plane when DreamWorks bought the script in March 2004
Score by Marco Beltrami
Released August 19, 2005
Lisa stabs Jackson in the throat with a ballpoint pen
Extended version broadcast on ABC

films.title: The Mummy Returns
films.basedOn: Characters by Sommers, Lloyd Fonvielle, Kevin Jarre
films.villain: Imhotep (Arnold Vosloo), resurrected by a cult led by Baltus Hafez; the Scorpion King
notes: Sequel to The Mummy (1999)
Dwayne Johnson (as The Rock) makes his film acting debut as the Scorpion King
Released May 4, 2001
Seventh-highest-grossing film of 2001; highest-grossing of the series
Followed by prequel The Scorpion King (2002)

films.title: Dagon
films.basedOn: H. P. Lovecraft's Dagon and The Shadow Over Innsmouth
films.villain: Half-fish villagers of Imboca who worship Dagon, led by cult founder Captain Orpheus Cambarro
notes: Spanish production in English, Galician and Spanish
Final Stuart Gordon / Dennis Paoli film collaboration
Imboca is the Spanish version of Lovecraft's Innsmouth
Francisco Rabal's final role; he died two months before release
Premiered at Sitges Film Festival Oct 12, 2001

films.title: Funny Games
films.yearNote: London Film Festival premiere Oct 20, 2007; US release March 14, 2008
films.basedOn: Funny Games (1997 film) by Michael Haneke
films.villain: Paul (Michael Pitt) and Peter (Brady Corbet), two young men who take a family hostage and torture them
notes: Shot-for-shot English-language remake of Haneke's own 1997 film
Also titled Funny Games U.S.
Exterior scenes filmed on Long Island
Only Haneke film not to premiere at Cannes
Mixed reviews and a commercial failure

films.title: Mulberry Street
films.yearNote: Festival premiere Nov 16, 2006; US theatrical Nov 9, 2007; direct-to-video March 18, 2008
films.villain: Rat-like zombie creatures created by a rat-borne infection spreading through Manhattan
notes: Made on a $60,000 budget; shot in three and a half weeks
Premiered at Stockholm International Film Festival Nov 16, 2006
Released by After Dark Films in the 8 Films to Die For lineup, Nov 9, 2007
Direct-to-video March 18, 2008
Also released as Zombie Virus on Mulberry Street
Creators wanted the title to emphasize gentrification

films.title: Wrong Turn 2: Dead End
films.yearNote: FrightFest premiere Aug 25, 2007; US DVD release Oct 9, 2007
films.villain: Family of deformed cannibals that hunt reality-show contestants
notes: Sequel to Wrong Turn (2003)
Premiered at FrightFest Aug 25, 2007; US DVD release Oct 9, 2007
Budget $4 million; $9.2M in home video sales
Best-reviewed film in the Wrong Turn series
Score by Bear McCreary
Followed by Wrong Turn 3: Left for Dead (2009)

films.title: Taking Lives
films.basedOn: Taking Lives (1999 novel) by Michael Pye
films.villain: Martin Asher, serial killer who assumes his victims' identities (revealed as art dealer James Costa)
notes: Loosely adapted from the 1999 novel
Released March 19, 2004
Score by Philip Glass
Generally negative reviews; moderate commercial success
Paul Dano plays young Martin Asher

films.title: The Happening
films.villain: Unexplained airborne toxin (theorized to come from plants) that drives people to mass suicide
notes: Shyamalan's first R-rated film
Premiered in New York City June 10, 2008; US release June 13
Half the budget financed by India's UTV Motion Pictures
Production began August 2007 in Philadelphia
Shyamalan described it as a 1960s paranoia film like The Birds and Invasion of the Body Snatchers
Negative reviews on release; later reappraised as a B movie

films.title: The Amityville Horror
films.basedOn: The Amityville Horror (novel) by Jay Anson
films.villain: Haunted house possessing George Lutz; spirit of cult preacher Reverend Jeremiah Ketcham
notes: Remake of the 1979 film; ninth film in the Amityville Horror series
Chloë Grace Moretz's film debut
Released April 15, 2005
Produced by Michael Bay, Andrew Form and Brad Fuller
Set on Long Island but shot in Illinois and Wisconsin
Negative reviews, commercial success

films.title: Hellraiser: Inferno
films.writers: Paul Harris Boardman and Scott Derrickson
films.villain: Pinhead (Doug Bradley), posing as psychiatrist Dr. Paul Gregory (James Remar)
notes: Fifth Hellraiser film and first released direct-to-video
Scott Derrickson's feature directorial debut
Released October 3, 2000
Thorne is a corrupt Denver detective who solves the puzzle box

films.title: Darkness
films.yearNote: Sitges premiere Oct 3, 2002; Spain Oct 11, 2002; US Dec 25, 2004
films.writers: Jaume Balagueró and Fernando de Felipe
films.villain: Satanic cult, including grandfather Albert, seeking to complete an eclipse ritual sacrificing children
notes: Spain/US co-production by Filmax and Dimension Films
Shot in Barcelona starting April 26, 2001
Premiered at Sitges Oct 3, 2002; released in Spain Oct 11, 2002
US release Dec 25, 2004 in an edited PG-13 cut (88 min vs 102 min)
Widely panned by critics but a commercial success
